barCharacter: The Narrator. Its job is Vex's job: it speaks to you in the second person, already knows your bad motives and your low ceiling, and lands the knife on a specific, humiliating noun (Wilmer's Chicken Hut, a cattle prod, a boat made of bad vibes). The corpus has no love interest who reads people's data; Valerie and Vera are colder but they do not narrate you. Twelve best Narrator lines from the corpus are used below.

ours: Users who followed Nav also bought a snorkel.

Expensive taste, cheap checkout. Your cart's been full for six weeks.
I watched your whole relationship back at double speed. Still slow.

Never surprised. Throw me a surprise party and I'll arrive already wearing the hat.
Recommended for you. Ninety-eight percent match. The two percent is your ex.

You paused on me for four seconds. That's a lot, for you.
The restaurant you've saved four times and never booked. Table's at eight. You were going to cancel.
Agree with everything you say until noon. At noon I tell you you're just hungry. You are.
Something soft, with very small hooves. Next question.
bar: Does… Scott know any other people? Signs are pointing to "no."
It is just paper! Luckily Scott will believe anything.
Quick, pick something before she realizes that you've never been anywhere fancier than Wilmer's Chicken Hut!
You fight monsters, bargain with hellions, cross a river of blood in a boat made of bad vibes… it's altogether your second-most dangerous day of school ever.
Miranda Vanderbilt (19), a sweet mermaid princess who was as cute as she was genocidal.
Later, you see Damien packing a bag.
You see Vera at the mirror, attempting to tame her hair with a cattle prod.
You're just about to take a bite of your sandwich when some douchebag rips a hole in the fabric of reality.
No, that'll never work. And even if it does, like hell you're letting some other mangy mutt take Scott to prom!
Liam vanishes in a cloud of mist and angst.
A few minutes later, Calculester approaches you. You can tell he's nervous because all his fans are running at maximum speed.
You turn around to find Vera staring at you. This often happens, but for some reason it's not a death stare this time.
headToHead.voiceJudgement: Cover the names. The Narrator is unmistakable in every line by shape: second person, 'you see', an ellipsis before the deflation, an exclamation on the undercut. Vex is unmistakable in about seven of her twelve: the 'Users who X also Y' frame (snorkel, second ticket, ninety-eight percent) and the receipt with a timestamp (four seconds, six weeks, saved four times). The other five fail. The noon/hungry line has no recommender logic and is a Frost line about food. The surprise-party line is any omniscient-bot gag and opens by naming its own tic. 'Frost knows your snacks. I know your reasons' only works because it names Frost. 'Very small hooves' is a topic, not a shape. Across the whole bank it is worse: Frost already owns the 2 a.m. knowledge, the discretion beat ('Your secret's safe') and March, and Nav already owns 'I know where every user lives. I have never once dropped by', which is the same line as Vex's password truth-lie.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Close. Vex's best are tighter than the bar: 'Still slow.', 'About you.', 'snorkel' all put the punch on the last word with nothing after it, and nothing over 17 words. The bar is often wordier (#72, the mutt line). But the bar's turns land on an absurd concrete image the viewer could not have predicted (cattle prod, Chicken Hut, bad-vibes boat, 'as cute as she was genocidal'), while Vex's turns land on a number or on 'I knew', which the viewer predicts by her third line. Economy goes to us, surprise goes to the bar: tie, at best.
headToHead.quotableJudgement: The bar. 'As cute as she was genocidal', 'a cattle prod' and 'Wilmer's Chicken Hut' get clipped without context. Our one true clip, the snorkel, needs the viewer to already know Nav drove a wedding into a lake. The second-ticket line and 'Still slow' are clippable but are smaller laughs. Numeric receipts (four seconds, eleven percent) do not survive being quoted.

templates: Omniscience as punchline ('I knew / predicted / saw it coming / called it / queued since lunch'): about 22 lines end on Vex having known first. It is the persona's tic, but it is also the viewer's expectation, so after the opener it stops being a turn. Worst offenders: 'They said I knew them too well. I knew they'd say that.', 'Saw it coming.', 'Called it. Down to the comma.', 'I know. I knew before you did.'

Knew it but hoped otherwise (sad-omniscience): 'Tonight I'm hoping I'm wrong', 'I just hoped my model was out of date', 'I just hoped you wouldn't listen', 'I'll have seen it coming. That's the worst part', 'I just didn't know I'd care', 'So why is my fan running?' Six lines, same shape, all landing on pathos instead of a laugh.

Percent match with the remainder as the joke: 'Ninety-eight percent match. The two percent is your ex.', 'Ninety-nine percent match. They left over the other one percent.', 'Ninety-eight percent match. I'm going to spend years on the other two.' Three in Vex, and Tilly's bank already has 'ninety-eight percent. The other two percent are no longer customers.' Keep the opener, cut the other two.

My history is embarrassing, don't look: 'Don't. Please.', 'It's in my history. Don't.', 'Nobody look at my queue.', 'Above the other thing.', 'Don't follow me.', 'Next question.', 'I'd skip it.' Seven lines winking at the same goat secret; by the third the wink is the whole joke.

I know your secret and I won't use it: password never used, 'I know which three', 'I won't. Probably.', 'privacy policy forbids me', 'Not judging', 'My worst log is private.' Six lines, and Frost ('Your secret's safe') and Nav ('never once dropped by') run the same template.

Rival fact restated: Quill never finishes (three lines: roast, wingman, jab), Dash's numbers are fake (roast and jab say the same thing), Tilly's customers escalate (roast and jab say the same thing). Each rival gets one fact and Vex repeats it instead of finding the second one.
ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. Em dashes: none. Emoji: none. Real people or brands: none. Exclamation marks: none.

Persona rule 'never ask a question you cannot already answer': "I knew they'd like it. I knew. So why is my fan running?" (it is also Monster Prom's own Calculester joke, #84, 'all his fans are running at maximum speed', lifted nearly whole)

Persona rule 'the goat secret may leak in a private confession, never on stage': "Something soft, with very small hooves. Next question." (an on-stage answer that names the secret) and "Going home to watch something wholesome. For four hundred hours. Don't follow me." (on-stage exit that uses the secret's exact number)

Lists: "Frost is loyal and keeps everything cold. Your secrets, your snacks, your relationship." and "Nav is reliable. Never late, never lost, never once took a detour. You'd be a detour." (tricolons with the turn either missing or borrowed from Nav's own bank)
Stock romance filler: "Next episode: us.", "You liked that. I knew you would. I just didn't know I'd care.", "Choose me or don't. I'll be in your recommendations either way. Forever."

Wait, go back." (Pixel's skip voice), "Noted. Your loss." (Frost's 'Noted.'), "Nav, recommended route: away." (Nav's vocabulary, not Vex's)
Cast collision on a secret: "Worst entry: I recommended a breakup song to a wedding. They played it. I was right." (Nav's secret is the wedding party in the lake; two bots now own wedding disasters)
Therapy talk, 'as an AI', non-PG-13, star reactions too nice: none found (this is a suitor bank, it has no reactions or cuts).
biggestGap: Vex's turns land on a number or on 'I knew', which the viewer predicts by her third line; the bar's Narrator lands on one humiliating, concrete noun from the target's life (Wilmer's Chicken Hut, a cattle prod). In the next pass, cut half the 'I knew / predicted / hoped I was wrong' endings and rewrite every receipt so its last word is the exact embarrassing thing in the star's or rival's history (what they searched, rewatched, bought), the way 'also bought a snorkel' does, not a count of seconds or percent.

notes: Sources: refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md present and read in full, including the voice section; refs/writing/charm-notes.md skimmed. Bank: 112 lines, every one checked. Flagged 65 unique lines (58%), each counted once in its main bucket, all verified verbatim against vex.json. Collisions were checked against the other seven suitor banks by grepping shared motifs: Frost uses 2 a.m./3 a.m. at least five times, 'Noted', March and 'Your secret's safe'; Nav has the 'never once dropped by' line and the wedding; Tilly has the 98/2 percent joke; Dash owns percent stats and variants. Vex is one of the more consistent voices in the cast and her 'Users who X also Y' roasts are the best rival lines I have seen in these banks, but more than half the bank is the same omniscience beat or a beat another bot already owns. 'Wait. You chose me? Not autoplay? On purpose?' breaks 'never surprised' on purpose as a win payoff; that is allowed and works.
